text:
devbot: Incident detected: elevated 5xx from dedicated-pool-tailwind-1 for tenant tailwind (fn_call parser failures) :rotating_light:
liam_oncall: paging oncall — I'm seeing alerts for fn_call errors, 25% error rate on tailwind's dedicated pool. logs show parser rejecting tool calls with SchemaValidationError
sara_ops: oncall here. any customer impact?
liam_oncall: Support report from jana says failures started ~11m ago, customers hitting failed tool calls in production (error: "Parser expected 'tool_id' but got null"). tailwind reported timeouts and partial responses.
jana_support: confirmed — they see failures for function calling only, plain generation OK. They're routing business-critical requests through our dedicated pool.
ops-bot: Added tag: priority=high, impacted=tailwind, service=fn-call-parser
anita_eng: quick hypothesis: recent parser upgrade (v3.4.1) rolled to the dedicated pool last night. Could be stricter schema validation.
mike_sre: logs from parser service on node gpux-03 show repeated stacktraces: 
```
errors.SchemaValidationError: Missing required property: tool_id
  at Object.validate (/srv/parser/validators.js:88:15)
  at parseFnCall (/srv/parser/index.js:142:21)
```
liam_oncall: Is this isolated to tailwind's dedicated pool or broader?
anita_eng: Preliminary cluster-wide sampling shows only dedicated-pool-tailwind-1 nodes saw v3.4.1; hosted clusters still on v3.3.8. Looks like a pinned rollout went to that pool.
sara_ops: mitigation plan? We should avoid customer-facing downtime. Options: rollback parser on pool, enable tolerant parsing flag for tenant, or route tailwind traffic to a compatible fallback model/variant.
mike_sre: I can rollback parser on gpux nodes. Rolling restart will briefly drop in-flight requests. For tailwind SLA we should try a per-tenant config toggle first.
anita_eng: There's a tenant-level feature flag service. We can flip `fncall_relaxed_schema` to true for tailwind which will accept missing tool_id and fallback to legacy behavior. Doing that avoids a restart.
liam_oncall: do it. Sara, can you coordinate with support to warn the customer? Jana, prep the message.
sara_ops: toggling feature now via admin console -> tenant-config -> tailwind -> set fncall_relaxed_schema = true :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Feature flag updated for tenant tailwind by sara_ops
anita_eng: Confirming parser logs show schema validation bypassed, error rate dropping to 1.8%
mike_sre: Good. I'll schedule a safe rollout rollback of v3.4.1 on dedicated-pool-tailwind-1 to v3.3.8 in 15m, with canary on gpux-04 first. If rollback succeeds we can re-enable strict schema.
liam_oncall: Jana, what did you tell the customer?
jana_support: Sent to tailwind: "We've identified a function-call parser regression affecting dedicated pools after a recent parser update. We've enabled a temporary compatibility flag for your tenant to restore traffic immediately and are rolling back the parser on your dedicated pool. We'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline." They acknowledged, asked for ETA.
sara_ops: ETA for rollback?
mike_sre: Canary starts in 5m. If metrics look good (error <0.5% and no latency spike) I'll promote. Plan includes rolling restarts one node at a time, draining connections first. Total expected impact: a few seconds per node, but we keep routing to other nodes during drain.
liam_oncall: I'll stay on the thread for handoff. If rollback succeeds, we close incident. If not, escalate to emergency rollback of model routing.
anita_eng: Root cause notes to collect: stricter validation introduced in v3.4.1, no canary on tenant-scoped dedicated pools, missing test coverage for legacy tool payloads. We'll capture failing payload samples and add to regression tests.
devbot: Incident created: INC-2026-8345, severity=P2, assigned=[mike_sre, anita_eng, liam_oncall]
mike_sre: Canary promoted — gpux-04 -> v3.3.8. Monitoring: error rate dropped to 0.2% for canary node. Promoting to gpux-03 now.
liam_oncall: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Node gpux-03 rolled back successfully
anita_eng: After rollback and flag still on, overall error rate for tailwind is <0.1%. We should keep fncall_relaxed_schema enabled until we've validated a test-suite run and updated parser to accept legacy payloads explicitly.
sara_ops: I'll set follow-up tasks: notify customer when flag is removed, schedule postmortem meeting, and coordinate patch release timeline. Jana — please collect customer impact details (times, request ids) for billing or SLA credits.
jana_support: On it — collecting request ids and affected endpoints.
liam_oncall: Ok team — I'll hand off to sara_ops for post-incident follow-up in 30m. If anything regresses ping with the INC ID.
sara_ops: taking over. Thanks all. Will draft postmortem stub and include payload examples. :eyes:
